title: 9.6 Permutations and Combinations

icans: I can count the ways to arrange objects using factorials.
I can find permutations and combinations and tell which one to use.
I can use permutations and combinations to find probabilities.

vocab: n!/(n − r)!, the number of _______________ of r objects chosen from n
a ____________ in which order does not matter
n!/((n − r)! · r!), the number of _______________ of r objects chosen from n

blocks.p: Your group is A, B, C, and D.
1. List every way to choose a president and a vice president (write president first).
2. List every way to choose a 2-person committee.
How many in each list? ________ and ________. Why is one list twice as long?

blocks.sec: Part 2 · Notes and examples (fill in each note, then work the example)

blocks.stem:
a.  In how many ways can you arrange the letters in MATH?
b.  In how many ways can you arrange 2 of the letters?
Ten runners are in a race. In how many ways can the gold, silver, and bronze medals be awarded?
A pizza shop has 8 toppings. How many different 3-topping pizzas can you order?

From a club of 12 members, how many ways can you
a.  choose a 4-member committee?
b.  choose a captain and a co-captain?
A class has 5 boys and 7 girls. Three students are chosen at random to present. What is the probability that all three are girls?

a.  In how many ways can 6 books be arranged on a shelf?
b.  In how many ways can 3 of the 6 books be arranged?
A pizza shop offers 10 toppings. How many different 3-topping pizzas are possible?

tickets.stem: In how many ways can 5 people line up?
In how many ways can a president, vice president, and secretary be chosen from 9 club members?
